A day has a beginning,
a middle, and a place to end.

Daymark brings the parts of a daybook together around what you meant to do, what you did, and what you want to carry into tomorrow.

Plan the day.

Today puts the next event first, then your tasks and rituals. Add a task or check in on a ritual without opening another page.

1 / 6

  1. 1 / 6

    A brief, when you want one.

    Tap Brief for what is next, what is open, the rituals kept, and today’s focus, with Ask Daymark one tap away.

    The sheet puts the next event and its time beside the task, ritual, and focus totals. You can ask a follow-up without leaving it.

  2. 2 / 6

    The forecast beside the plans.

    The selected city’s Apple Weather forecast appears above tasks and events for the day.

    Conditions live in the context of your schedule. There is no separate weather page to consult before making a plan.

  3. 3 / 6

    See the day in hours.

    Open the day to see events laid out in time, and step through the week from the strip above.

    An hourly view shows where commitments sit in relation to one another; the week strip makes moving to another day feel immediate.

  4. 4 / 6

    Find a day in the month.

    Days with events carry a mark. Tap one to open it.

    Pull back from the details to see the shape of a month, then return directly to the day you want to explore.

  5. 5 / 6

    Every task in one list.

    Open tasks are grouped by day. Finished ones fold away under Done.

    The next actions stay visible without losing the record of what you already finished. It is a list designed to be revisited.

  6. 6 / 6

    Give a task its time.

    Block time for a task with a start and a length. It lands in the daybook, and on your Apple calendar once you import a writable one.

    The sheet lets you set a date, start time, and duration before adding the block. Calendar write-back depends on the calendar you selected.

Swipe to explore. Each card is numbered.

Keep a practice.

Set a daily, weekday, or weekly rhythm, then review check-ins across the week.

  1. Check in across the week.

    Use daily, weekday, or weekly cadences. Check in from Today or from the Rituals page.

    A simple ledger makes the rhythm of a practice visible. Missed days stay part of the story without obscuring the days you kept.

Protect your attention.

Give one task a protected block of time, then see where today’s focus went.

1 / 4

  1. 1 / 4

    One dial, one task.

    Run a Pomodoro with focus, short rest, and long rest, or pick a 25, 50, or 90 minute session.

    Set a deliberate boundary around your work, with rest built into the rhythm when you choose Pomodoro.

  2. 2 / 4

    Timers and countdowns.

    Keep reusable timers for the things you do often, and count down to the dates ahead.

    A familiar timer can be started again, while a countdown gives important future dates a place in the daybook.

  3. 3 / 4

    See where the time went.

    Focus history keeps the last seven days and today’s sessions in one ledger.

    Look back across the week and see individual sessions beneath the daily totals. Time spent becomes something you can reflect on.

  4. 4 / 4

    Focus comes with you.

    A running session stays in view while you move to another page.

    You can glance at the session while using another part of Daymark, without abandoning the work you started.

Swipe to explore. Each card is numbered.

Review what mattered.

Weekly Review gathers completed tasks, focus sessions, and ritual check-ins from the week you recorded.

  1. A week you can see.

    Tasks done, focus minutes, and rituals kept come together beside three prompts: what mattered, what got in the way, and one change for next week.

    The totals are drawn from the week you recorded. Add your own answers beneath the prompts to keep a record of what you want to repeat or change.

Keep what deserves to stay.

Notes, links, and images in one place. Share from another app and it lands on the Shelf the next time you open Daymark.

1 / 3

  1. 1 / 3

    Filter by kind or tag.

    Pin what should stay on top, and tag entries so they are easy to gather again.

    Collect the small things you want to remember and give them just enough structure to find them later.

  2. 2 / 3

    A note, ready to return to.

    Copy it, share it, edit it, or move it to Recently deleted. Entries can be restored there for 30 days.

    A saved thought stays editable, portable, and recoverable for a time when you decide it no longer belongs on the Shelf.

  3. 3 / 3

    Find anything in the daybook.

    Search tasks, events, Shelf entries, rituals, and weekly reviews. Spotlight indexing is optional.

    Move across the kinds of information in your daybook from one search, without remembering which page holds the answer.

Swipe to explore. Each card is numbered.

Ask about your day.

Ask Daymark answers from your daybook and makes typed, explainable changes. It works offline, with or without the optional model.

1 / 4

  1. 1 / 4

    A brief from the day you have.

    Ask for the day’s shape and get an answer from the events, tasks, rituals, focus, and weather already in Daymark.

    The answer is informed by the records already in your daybook, so a question can become a useful place to begin.

  2. 2 / 4

    From phrase to typed action.

    With the optional Gemma 4 model, a loose sentence can produce a typed action and reviewable receipt. Daymark validates and writes the change.

    The model interprets the request, but the app remains responsible for validating the action before it becomes part of your daybook.

  3. 3 / 4

    Grounded by default.

    In Daybook mode, answers come from your actual day, and each reply is tagged with the mode that wrote it.

    The visible mode helps distinguish answers drawn from your records from an open-ended conversation.

  4. 4 / 4

    Open conversation, on request.

    Switch to Open chat for general questions. Web search is off unless you turn it on.

    General conversation is available separately from daybook questions, with network search remaining an explicit choice.

Swipe to explore. Each card is numbered.

Yours to set.

Daymark starts empty and stays quiet until you ask for more.

1 / 5

  1. 1 / 5

    It starts empty.

    A fresh install holds nothing of yours. Explore a sample day to see the loop, then choose Start fresh to clear it.

    Try the experience with clearly labeled example content, without carrying those examples into a fresh daybook.

  2. 2 / 5

    Choose the paper.

    Pick a paper tone and an accent, or let Daylight move the page with the sun.

    A fixed tone stays in place. Daylight changes between paper tones around sunrise and sunset in the selected weather city, when available.

  3. 3 / 5

    Reminders you opt into.

    A morning brief, due tasks, ritual nudges, and event alerts. Each one is off until you turn it on.

    Choose which kinds of prompts deserve permission to interrupt your day; silence remains the starting point.

  4. 4 / 5

    Your calendar, live.

    Connect Apple Calendar and Reminders, then choose the calendars and lists Daymark reads. Edits save back to those accounts.

    You select the sources Daymark can use, while the underlying calendar and reminder accounts remain managed by the system.

  5. 5 / 5

    Keep a copy, or start again.

    Import or export tasks, events, and Shelf entries. Spotlight is optional. Erase Daymark data has its own confirmation.

    Data controls are explicit. The limited export covers the named record types, and erasing the daybook requires a deliberate confirmation.

Private by default. Clear about the exceptions.

Daymark has no account, analytics, cloud sync, or remote AI service. A few optional connections belong to features you choose to use.

Your daybookStored in Daymark on this device.

Web searchOff by default. Only your question is sent when you search.

Calendar and RemindersUses the system accounts and lists you select.

Weather and linksConnect to providers only when those features are used.
